objective.text: Append a computed accessor to output without treating it as a database column.

difficulty.rationale: Separate serialization-time computation from the table schema.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: Customer appends full_name through an accessor that joins first_name and last_name. The table has those two columns but no full_name column. Why does Customer::select("full_name")->get() fail even though full_name appears in toArray()?

options.text: Appending affects serialization; the query must select the source columns needed by the accessor.
options.rationale: An accessor is computed in PHP and appends does not add a SQL column to the database table.

options.text: The accessor must be renamed to getFullNameAttribute to become a SQL column.
options.rationale: Neither accessor naming convention creates a physical or generated SQL column.
options.misconception: Neither accessor naming convention creates a physical or generated SQL column.

options.text: Appending requires full_name to be placed in $fillable before selecting it.
options.rationale: Fillable controls mass assignment, not SQL schema or projection.
options.misconception: Fillable controls mass assignment, not SQL schema or projection.

options.text: select disables every accessor permanently on the model class.
options.rationale: Selecting columns does not remove accessor methods; the invalid database column is the immediate problem.
options.misconception: Selecting columns does not remove accessor methods; the invalid database column is the immediate problem.
